s: day of trumpets (first day of seventh month) is a solemn rest and memorial of trumpet blowing (holy convocation)
q: In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, there shall be a solemn rest for you, a memorial of blowing of trumpets, a holy convocation.

s: day of atonement occurs on tenth day of seventh month (holy convocation)
q: on the tenth day of this seventh month is the day of atonement. It shall be a holy convocation to you.

s: set feasts of the LORD belongs to the LORD
q: The set feasts of the LORD, which you shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my set feasts.

s: day of atonement purpose make atonement before the LORD (no work allowed)
q: for it is a day of atonement, to make atonement for you before the LORD your God.

s: day of atonement requires self-denial (whoever does not is cut off from his people)
q: For whoever it is who shall not deny himself in that same day shall be cut off from his people.

s: day of atonement is a Sabbath of solemn rest (statute forever, kept evening to evening)
q: It shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest for you, and you shall deny yourselves.

s: feast of booths occurs on fifteenth day of seventh month (lasts seven days)
q: On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the feast of booths for seven days to the LORD.

s: feast of booths has solemn assembly on eighth day (no regular work)
q: On the eighth day shall be a holy convocation to you. You shall offer an offering made by fire to the LORD. It is a solemn assembly; you shall do no regular work.

s: feast of booths is a statute forever (kept in the seventh month)
q: It is a statute forever throughout your generations. You shall keep it in the seventh month.

s: feast of booths requires dwelling in temporary shelters (seven days, all native-born in Israel)
q: You shall dwell in temporary shelters for seven days.

s: feast of booths commemorates dwelling in shelters after leaving Egypt
q: that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in temporary shelters when I brought them out of the land of Egypt.

s: offerings is in addition to Sabbaths, gifts, vows, free will offerings (feast offerings each on its own day)
q: in addition to the Sabbaths of the LORD, and in addition to your gifts, and in addition to all your vows, and in addition to all your free will offerings, which you give to the LORD.

s: the LORD speaks to Moses (gives instructions on feasts)
q: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

s: Sabbath is a solemn rest (holy convocation on the seventh day)
q: but on the seventh day is a Sabbath of solemn rest, a holy convocation; you shall do no kind of work.

s: the LORD is god of children of Israel
q: I am the LORD your God.’”

s: the LORD brought out of egypt children of Israel
q: when I brought them out of the land of Egypt.

s: Moses declares feasts to children of Israel
q: So Moses declared to the children of Israel the appointed feasts of the LORD.

s: children of Israel must leave gleanings for poor and foreigner (not reaping field corners)
q: you must not wholly reap into the corners of your field. You must not gather the gleanings of your harvest. You must leave them for the poor and for the foreigner.

s: Sabbath applies in all dwellings (Sabbath to the LORD)
q: It is a Sabbath to the LORD in all your dwellings.

s: Passover occurs on fourteenth day of first month, in the evening
q: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month in the evening, is the LORD’s Passover.

s: feast of unleavened bread occurs on fifteenth day of first month
q: On the fifteenth day of the same month is the feast of unleavened bread to the LORD.

s: feast of unleavened bread lasts seven days (unleavened bread eaten)
q: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.

s: feast of unleavened bread has holy convocation on first day (no regular work)
q: In the first day you shall have a holy convocation. You shall do no regular work.

s: offering of the first fruits sheaf is waved by priest (before the LORD, on the day after the Sabbath)
q: He shall wave the sheaf before the LORD, to be accepted for you. On the next day after the Sabbath the priest shall wave it.

s: Aaron keeps in order lamp stand (from evening to morning before the LORD continually)
q: He shall keep in order the lamps on the pure gold lamp stand before the LORD continually.

s: stoning of the blasphemer is carried out by children of Israel (outside the camp, as the LORD commanded Moses)
q: they brought him who had cursed out of the camp, and stoned him with stones. The children of Israel did as the LORD commanded Moses.

s: law of retribution prescribes fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth (done to him as he has injured someone)
q: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. It shall be done to him as he has injured someone.

s: law of retribution applies to foreigner (one law for foreigner and native-born)
q: You shall have one kind of law for the foreigner as well as the native-born; for I am the LORD your God.

s: Aaron receives twelve cakes (shared with his sons; eaten in a holy place)
q: It shall be for Aaron and his sons. They shall eat it in a holy place;

s: olive oil for the lamp is provided by children of Israel (pure, beaten for the light)
q: Command the children of Israel, that they bring to you pure olive oil beaten for the light, to cause a lamp to burn continually.

s: son of the Israelite woman has mother Shelomith
q: His mother’s name was Shelomith, the daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.

s: son of the Israelite woman has father nationality Egyptian
q: The son of an Israelite woman, whose father was an Egyptian,

s: blasphemy of the Name has penalty death by stoning (applies to foreigner and native-born alike)
q: He who blasphemes the LORD’s name, he shall surely be put to death. All the congregation shall certainly stone him. The foreigner as well as the native-born shall be put to death when he blasphemes the Name.

s: Sabbath year occurs in seventh year (every seven years)
q: but in the seventh year there shall be a Sabbath of solemn rest for the land, a Sabbath to the LORD.

s: land (land given to Israel) owned by the LORD (Israelites are strangers and foreigners with him)
q: The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine; for you are strangers and live as foreigners with me.

s: land (land given to Israel) cannot be sold in perpetuity
q: The land shall not be sold in perpetuity, for the land is mine

s: land (land given to Israel) is given to children of Israel (by the LORD)
q: When you come into the land which I give you, then the land shall keep a Sabbath to the LORD.

s: the LORD is god of children of Israel
q: for I am the LORD your God.

s: the LORD brought out of Egypt (the children of Israel)
q: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.

s: the LORD gives land of Canaan (to the children of Israel)
q: who brought you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.

s: children of Israel are servants of the LORD
q: For to me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.

s: poor brother has right to land redemption (redeemed by nearest kinsman or himself if prosperous)
q: If your brother becomes poor, and sells some of his possessions, then his kinsman who is next to him shall come, and redeem that which his brother has sold.

s: poor brother is treated as alien or temporary resident (when upheld by fellow Israelite)
q: then you shall uphold him. He shall live with you like an alien and a temporary resident.

s: poor brother is protected from interest (no interest or profit taken)
q: Take no interest from him or profit; but fear your God, that your brother may live among you.

s: Sabbath year prohibits sowing and pruning (for the land)
q: You shall not sow your field or prune your vineyard.

s: poor brother serves as hired servant (not as slave, until Year of Jubilee)
q: As a hired servant, and as a temporary resident, he shall be with you; he shall serve with you until the Year of Jubilee.

s: poor brother is released in Year of Jubilee (with his children)
q: Then he shall go out from you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own family, and to the possession of his fathers.

s: land redemption is required for land (land given to Israel) (throughout all possessed land)
q: In all the land of your possession you shall grant a redemption for the land.

s: land redemption is calculated by years since sale (surplus restored to buyer)
q: then let him reckon the years since its sale, and restore the surplus to the man to whom he sold it; and he shall return to his property.

s: Sabbath year provides food for servants (land's produce is food for household, servants, hired servants and strangers)
q: The Sabbath of the land shall be for food for you; for yourself, for your servant, for your maid, for your hired servant, and for your stranger, who lives as a foreigner with you.

s: interest-free lending applies to poor brother (no interest on money or food)
q: You shall not lend him your money at interest, nor give him your food for profit.

s: Sabbath year provides food for livestock (all the land's increase)
q: For your livestock also, and for the animals that are in your land, shall all its increase be for food.

s: Year of Jubilee occurs in fiftieth year (after seven Sabbaths of years)
q: You shall make the fiftieth year holy, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all its inhabitants.

s: Year of Jubilee begins on day of atonement (announced by loud trumpet on tenth day of seventh month)
q: Then you shall sound the loud trumpet on the tenth day of the seventh month. On the Day of Atonement you shall sound the trumpet throughout all your land.

s: Year of Jubilee is holy
q: For it is a jubilee; it shall be holy to you.

s: Year of Jubilee requires return to own property and family (for each person)
q: It shall be a jubilee to you; and each of you shall return to his own property, and each of you shall return to his family.

s: Year of Jubilee prohibits sowing and reaping (including self-grown produce and undressed vines)
q: In it you shall not sow, neither reap that which grows of itself, nor gather from the undressed vines.

s: the LORD is god of children of Israel
q: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.

s: the LORD does not utterly reject children of Israel (even when they are in enemy lands)
q: Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly and to break my covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God.

s: the LORD made statutes through Moses (at Mount Sinai)
q: These are the statutes, ordinances, and laws, which the LORD made between him and the children of Israel in Mount Sinai by Moses.

s: children of Israel forbidden to make idols (also carved images, pillars, figured stones)
q: You shall make for yourselves no idols, and you shall not raise up a carved image or a pillar, and you shall not place any figured stone in your land, to bow down to it

s: children of Israel commanded to keep Sabbath
q: You shall keep my Sabbaths, and have reverence for my sanctuary.

s: children of Israel commanded to revere sanctuary
q: You shall keep my Sabbaths, and have reverence for my sanctuary.

s: sanctuary belongs to the LORD
q: You shall keep my Sabbaths, and have reverence for my sanctuary.

s: Sabbath belongs to the LORD
q: You shall keep my Sabbaths, and have reverence for my sanctuary.

s: blessings for obedience includes rain in season and abundant harvests (condition: walking in statutes and keeping commandments)
q: If you walk in my statutes and keep my commandments, and do them, 4 then I will give you your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit

s: blessings for obedience includes peace in the land (no fear, no sword, evil animals removed)
q: I will give peace in the land, and you shall lie down, and no one will make you afraid. I will remove evil animals out of the land, neither shall the sword go through your land.

s: blessings for obedience includes victory over enemies (five chase a hundred)
q: Five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand; and your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.

s: children of Israel is people of the LORD
q: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.

s: blessings for obedience includes fruitfulness and multiplication
q: I will have respect for you, make you fruitful, multiply you, and will establish my covenant with you.

s: punishments for disobedience includes terror, consumption and fever (first stage, for rejecting statutes and breaking covenant)
q: I will appoint terror over you, even consumption and fever, that shall consume the eyes, and make the soul to pine away.

s: punishments for disobedience includes rule by enemies (Israelites flee when no one pursues)
q: Those who hate you will rule over you; and you will flee when no one pursues

s: punishments for disobedience includes sky like iron and soil like bronze (second stage, sevenfold)
q: I will make your sky like iron, and your soil like bronze.

s: punishments for disobedience includes wild animals (third stage, rob children and destroy livestock)
q: I will send the wild animals among you, which will rob you of your children, destroy your livestock, and make you few in number.

s: punishments for disobedience includes sword, pestilence and famine (fourth stage)
q: I will bring a sword upon you that will execute the vengeance of the covenant.

s: punishments for disobedience includes cannibalism (fifth stage)
q: You will eat the flesh of your sons, and you will eat the flesh of your daughters.

s: punishments for disobedience includes scattering among the nations
q: I will scatter you among the nations, and I will draw out the sword after you.

s: punishments for disobedience escalates sevenfold (each stage if Israelites do not listen)
q: If you in spite of these things will not listen to me, then I will chastise you seven times more for your sins.

s: the LORD destroys high places and incense altars (as punishment)
q: I will destroy your high places, and cut down your incense altars, and cast your dead bodies upon the bodies of your idols; and my soul will abhor you.

s: the LORD brought out of egypt children of Israel (freed them from slavery)
q: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, that you should not be their slaves.

s: the LORD lays waste cities (as punishment)
q: I will lay your cities waste, and will bring your sanctuaries to desolation.

s: the land (Israel's land) enjoys Sabbath (while desolate and Israelites are in exile)
q: Then the land will enjoy its Sabbaths as long as it lies desolate and you are in your enemies’ land.

s: the land (Israel's land) has state desolation (under punishment)
q: I will bring the land into desolation, and your enemies who dwell in it will be astonished at it.

s: children of Israel are scattered among nations (punishment for disobedience)
q: I will scatter you among the nations, and I will draw out the sword after you.

s: covenant is with ancestors (brought out of Egypt; the LORD remembers it for their sake)
q: But I will for their sake remember the covenant of their ancestors, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, that I might be their God.

s: enemies fall before children of Israel (when Israelites obey)
q: You shall chase your enemies, and they shall fall before you by the sword.

s: children of Israel confess iniquity for restoration covenant (humbled uncircumcised hearts lead the LORD to remember the covenant)
q: if then their uncircumcised heart is humbled, and they then accept the punishment of their iniquity, 42 then I will remember my covenant with Jacob

s: the LORD broke yoke of Israelites' slavery (made them walk upright)
q: I have broken the bars of your yoke, and made you walk upright.

s: the LORD establishes covenant (with the Israelites, if obedient)
q: I will have respect for you, make you fruitful, multiply you, and will establish my covenant with you.

s: the LORD sets tent among children of Israel (blessing for obedience)
q: I will set my tent among you, and my soul won’t abhor you.

s: the LORD remembers covenant with Abraham (when the Israelites confess and humble themselves)
q: then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham; and I will remember the land.

s: the LORD remembers covenant with Isaac (when the Israelites confess and humble themselves)
q: then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham; and I will remember the land.

s: the LORD remembers covenant with Jacob (when the Israelites confess and humble themselves)
q: then I will remember my covenant with Jacob, my covenant with Isaac, and also my covenant with Abraham; and I will remember the land.

s: the LORD speaks to Moses (instructing him to relay to the children of Israel)
q: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

s: vow of consecrating persons and valuation values female aged 60 and up at ten shekels
q: if he is a male, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.

s: priest assigns value to vow of consecrating persons and valuation (for a person poorer than the valuation, according to ability to pay)
q: The priest shall assign a value according to his ability to pay.

s: animals dedicated to the LORD becomes holy (animals of a kind offered as offerings)
q: all that any man gives of such to the LORD becomes holy.

s: animals dedicated to the LORD cannot be exchanged (if exchanged, both animals become holy)
q: He shall not alter it, nor exchange it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good. If he shall at all exchange animal for animal, then both it and that for which it is exchanged shall be holy.

s: priest evaluates animals dedicated to the LORD (unclean animals not offered as offerings)
q: and the priest shall evaluate it, whether it is good or bad. As the priest evaluates it, so it shall be.

s: redemption (adding a fifth) requires adding fifth part of the valuation (when redeeming a dedicated unclean animal)
q: But if he will indeed redeem it, then he shall add the fifth part of it to its valuation.

s: house (dedicated house) is evaluated by priest (his valuation stands)
q: then the priest shall evaluate it, whether it is good or bad. As the priest evaluates it, so it shall stand.

s: house (dedicated house) is redeemed by adding fifth part of the valuation (and it then remains his)
q: then he shall add the fifth part of the money of your valuation to it, and it shall be his.

s: field (dedicated field) is valued at fifty shekels of silver per homer of barley sowing (valuation according to the seed)
q: The sowing of a homer of barley shall be valued at fifty shekels of silver.

s: field (dedicated field) has valuation reduced after Year of Jubilee (when dedicated after the Jubilee, by the years remaining)
q: But if he dedicates his field after the Jubilee, then the priest shall reckon to him the money according to the years that remain to the Year of Jubilee; and an abatement shall be made from your valuation.

s: Moses receives commandments on Mount Sinai (commandments for the children of Israel)
q: These are the commandments which the LORD commanded Moses for the children of Israel on Mount Sinai.

s: field (dedicated field) is owned by priests (if not redeemed or if sold, when it goes out in the Jubilee)
q: It shall be owned by the priests.

s: field (dedicated field) returns in jubilee to original seller (for a bought field dedicated by a buyer)
q: In the Year of Jubilee the field shall return to him from whom it was bought

s: animals dedicated to the LORD excludes firstborn animals (they belong to the LORD and cannot be dedicated)
q: However the firstborn among animals, which belongs to the LORD as a firstborn, no man may dedicate, whether an ox or a sheep. It is the LORD’s.

s: devoted things is most holy to the LORD (permanently devoted; cannot be sold or redeemed)
q: shall be sold or redeemed. Everything that is permanently devoted is most holy to the LORD.

s: devoted things cannot be ransomed (person devoted to destruction is put to death)
q: No one devoted to destruction, who shall be devoted from among men, shall be ransomed. He shall surely be put to death.

s: tithe belongs to the LORD (tithe of the land, seed and fruit; holy)
q: All the tithe of the land, whether of the seed of the land or of the fruit of the trees, is the LORD’s. It is holy to the LORD.

s: tithe requires adding when redeemed fifth part
q: If a man redeems anything of his tithe, he shall add a fifth part to it.

s: tithe includes as holy tenth of herds and flocks (whatever passes under the rod)
q: All the tithe of the herds or the flocks, whatever passes under the rod, the tenth shall be holy to the LORD.

s: tithe cannot be redeemed (animal tithe; no examining or exchanging)
q: It shall not be redeemed.

s: vow of consecrating persons and valuation values male aged 20 to 60 at fifty shekels of silver (according to the shekel of the sanctuary)
q: your valuation of a male from twenty years old to sixty years old shall be fifty shekels of silver, according to the shekel of the sanctuary.

s: vow of consecrating persons and valuation values female aged 20 to 60 at thirty shekels
q: If she is a female, then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.

s: vow of consecrating persons and valuation values male aged 5 to 20 at twenty shekels
q: then your valuation shall be for a male twenty shekels, and for a female ten shekels.

s: vow of consecrating persons and valuation values female aged 5 to 20 at ten shekels
q: then your valuation shall be for a male twenty shekels, and for a female ten shekels.

s: vow of consecrating persons and valuation values male aged 1 month to 5 years at five shekels of silver
q: then your valuation shall be for a male five shekels of silver, and for a female your valuation shall be three shekels of silver.

s: vow of consecrating persons and valuation values female aged 1 month to 5 years at three shekels of silver
q: then your valuation shall be for a male five shekels of silver, and for a female your valuation shall be three shekels of silver.

s: vow of consecrating persons and valuation values male aged 60 and up at fifteen shekels
q: if he is a male, then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels, and for a female ten shekels.

s: Aaron's sons is a priests
q: Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle the blood around on the altar.

s: lamb (offering from the flock) has sex male or female (flock offering)
q: If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD is from the flock, either male or female, he shall offer it without defect.

s: lamb (offering from the flock) has condition without defect (required)
q: If his offering for a sacrifice of peace offerings to the LORD is from the flock, either male or female, he shall offer it without defect.

s: lamb (offering from the flock) has part entire tail fat (removed close to the backbone)
q: its fat, the entire tail fat, he shall take away close to the backbone

s: lamb (offering from the flock) is killed at Tent of Meeting (before it)
q: and he shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it before the Tent of Meeting.

s: goat (offering) is killed at Tent of Meeting (before it)
q: He shall lay his hand on its head, and kill it before the Tent of Meeting;

s: goat (offering) is offered before the LORD
q: If his offering is a goat, then he shall offer it before the LORD.

s: fat belongs to the LORD (all the fat)
q: all the fat is the LORD’s.

s: perpetual statute against eating fat and blood prohibits eating fat (throughout generations, in all dwellings)
q: It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings, that you shall eat neither fat nor blood.

s: perpetual statute against eating fat and blood prohibits eating sacrificial blood (throughout generations, in all dwellings)
q: It shall be a perpetual statute throughout your generations in all your dwellings, that you shall eat neither fat nor blood.

s: altar hosts burnt offering (fat burned on the burnt offering on the wood)
q: Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar on the burnt offering, which is on the wood that is on the fire

s: Aaron's sons sprinkle blood on altar (around the altar, for herd offerings)
q: Aaron’s sons, the priests, shall sprinkle the blood around on the altar.

s: Aaron's sons burn on altar (the fat of the herd offering)
q: Aaron’s sons shall burn it on the altar on the burnt offering, which is on the wood that is on the fire

s: sacrifice of peace offerings is a offering made by fire (to the LORD)
q: He shall offer of the sacrifice of peace offerings an offering made by fire to the LORD.

s: sacrifice of peace offerings has aroma pleasant (to the LORD)
q: it is an offering made by fire, of a pleasant aroma to the LORD.

s: herd animal (offering from the herd) has sex male or female
q: if he offers it from the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without defect before the LORD.

s: herd animal (offering from the herd) has condition without defect (required)
q: if he offers it from the herd, whether male or female, he shall offer it without defect before the LORD.

s: herd animal (offering from the herd) is killed at Tent of Meeting (at the door)
q: He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

s: offerer (the person bringing the offering) lays hand on herd animal (offering from the herd) (on its head)
q: He shall lay his hand on the head of his offering, and kill it at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

s: anointed priest offers young bull (sin offering when he sins so as to bring guilt on the people)
q: if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin which he has sinned a young bull without defect to the LORD for a sin offering.

s: sin offering is killed at altar (place where the burnt offering is killed, for ruler and common people)
q: kill the sin offering in the place of burnt offering.

s: anointed priest makes atonement (for the assembly, ruler or individual; they are forgiven)
q: the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.

s: altar located at Tent of Meeting (at the door)
q: the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

s: altar of sweet incense located in Tent of Meeting
q: the altar of sweet incense before the LORD, which is in the Tent of Meeting

s: blood is poured at altar (the rest of the blood, at the base)
q: he shall pour out the rest of the blood of the bull at the base of the altar of burnt offering

s: blood is put on altar (on its horns, for ruler's goat)
q: put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering.

s: fat is burned on altar (removed as from peace offerings)
q: The priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.

s: unintentional sin is a sin against the LORD's commands (done unwittingly, against things the LORD commanded not to be done)
q: If anyone sins unintentionally, in any of the things which the LORD has commanded not to be done, and does any one of them

s: the LORD commands Moses (spoke to him)
q: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

s: young bull required condition without defect (sin offering for the anointed priest)
q: a young bull without defect to the LORD for a sin offering

s: whole congregation of Israel offers young bull (sin offering when the sin becomes known)
q: then the assembly shall offer a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.

s: ruler offers goat (ruler's offering) (sin offering when his sin is made known to him)
q: he shall bring as his offering a goat, a male without defect.

s: goat (ruler's offering) is a sin offering
q: It is a sin offering.

s: goat (ruler's offering) required sex male (without defect)
q: a goat, a male without defect.

s: common people offers goat (common person's offering) (sin offering when sin is made known)
q: then he shall bring for his offering a goat, a female without defect, for his sin which he has sinned.

s: the priest makes atonement (for the sinner concerning his sin)
q: and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin.

s: sinner (the person who sins) must make restitution (for wrong regarding holy things, plus a fifth part, given to the priest)
q: He shall make restitution for that which he has done wrong regarding the holy thing, and shall add a fifth part to it, and give it to the priest;

s: unwitting sin has status guilty (even though the person didn't know it)
q: though he didn’t know it, he is still guilty, and shall bear his iniquity.

s: unwitting sin is atoned by trespass offering (a ram without defect, brought to the priest)
q: He shall bring a ram without defect from of the flock, according to your estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning the thing in which he sinned and didn’t know it, and he will be forgiven.

s: the LORD speaks to Moses (giving the trespass offering laws)
q: The LORD spoke to Moses, saying,

s: sinner (the person who sins) must do confession (when guilty of one of these things)
q: he shall confess that in which he has sinned;

s: sinner (the person who sins) bears iniquity (if he does not report what he witnessed)
q: if he doesn’t report it, then he shall bear his iniquity.

s: sin offering consists of female lamb or goat (standard offering from the flock)
q: a female from the flock, a lamb or a goat, for a sin offering;

s: sin offering consists of turtledoves or young pigeons (if the sinner can't afford a lamb; one of two birds)
q: two turtledoves, or two young pigeons, to the LORD; one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering.

s: sin offering consists of fine flour offering (if the sinner can't afford birds; one tenth of an ephah, no oil or frankincense)
q: one tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering. He shall put no oil on it, and he shall not put any frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.

s: sin offering has blood sprinkled on altar (some on the side, the rest drained at the base)
q: He shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar; and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar.

s: the priest receives fine flour offering (the remainder after the memorial portion is burned)
q: and the rest shall be the priest’s, as the meal offering.

s: trespass offering consists of ram (without defect, for sin regarding the LORD's holy things or unknowing sin)
q: a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation in silver by shekels, according to the shekel of the sanctuary, for a trespass offering.

s: the LORD speaks to Moses (gives laws of offerings)

s: burnt offering remains on altar (on the hearth all night until morning)
q: the burnt offering shall be on the hearth on the altar all night until the morning;

s: altar fire burns continuously (must not go out)
q: Fire shall be kept burning on the altar continually; it shall not go out.

s: priest (Aaron's line) wears linen garment and linen trousers (while removing the altar ashes)
q: The priest shall put on his linen garment, and he shall put on his linen trousers upon his body;

s: priest (Aaron's line) burns wood on the altar (every morning)
q: the priest shall burn wood on it every morning.

s: meal offering is offered by Aaron's sons (before the LORD, before the altar)
q: the sons of Aaron shall offer it before the LORD, before the altar.

s: meal offering is not baked with yeast
q: It shall not be baked with yeast.

s: meal offering is most holy
q: It is most holy, as are the sin offering and the trespass offering.

s: meal offering is eaten by Aaron's sons (remainder after the memorial portion; every male, in a holy place)
q: That which is left of it Aaron and his sons shall eat.

s: sin offering is killed at place of the burnt offering (before the LORD)
q: in the place where the burnt offering is killed, the sin offering shall be killed before the LORD. It is most holy.

s: the LORD commands Aaron (via Moses, regarding the burnt offering law)
q: “Command Aaron and his sons, saying, ‘This is the law of the burnt offering:

s: sin offering is eaten by priest (Aaron's line) (the priest who offers it, in a holy place)
q: The priest who offers it for sin shall eat it.

s: sin offering is burned if blood brought into Tent of Meeting (not eaten)
q: No sin offering, of which any of the blood is brought into the Tent of Meeting to make atonement in the Holy Place, shall be eaten. It shall be burned with fire.

s: sin offering is most holy
q: It is most holy.

s: trespass against a neighbor is a sin against the LORD
q: “If anyone sins, and commits a trespass against the LORD, and deals falsely with his neighbor in a matter of deposit, or of bargain, or of robbery, or has oppressed his neighbor,

s: trespass against a neighbor includes lying about found lost property
q: or has found that which was lost, and lied about it, and swearing to a lie

s: sinner (offender) must make restitution (on being found guilty)
q: he shall restore that which he took by robbery, or the thing which he has gotten by oppression, or the deposit which was committed to him, or the lost thing which he found,

s: restitution includes addition a fifth part (added to the full amount)
q: he shall restore it in full, and shall add a fifth part more to it.

s: restitution is returned to owner (on the day of being found guilty)
q: He shall return it to him to whom it belongs in the day of his being found guilty.

s: trespass offering consists of ram without defect (from the flock)
q: a ram without defect from the flock, according to your estimation, for a trespass offering, to the priest.

s: trespass offering is most holy
q: It is most holy, as are the sin offering and the trespass offering.

s: trespass offering is a most holy offering
q: This is the law of the trespass offering: It is most holy.

s: peace offerings thanksgiving eating deadline day of offering (none may remain until morning)
q: The flesh of the sacrifice of his peace offerings for thanksgiving shall be eaten on the day of his offering. He shall not leave any of it until the morning.

s: peace offerings eating deadline on the day of offering, with remainder eaten the next day (vow or freewill offering)
q: it shall be eaten on the day that he offers his sacrifice. On the next day what remains of it shall be eaten,

s: peace offerings has portion for priests peace offerings (waved breast and heaved thigh) (breast waved, right thigh heaved, given to Aaron and sons forever)
q: For the waved breast and the heaved thigh I have taken from the children of Israel out of the sacrifices of their peace offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as their portion forever from the children of Israel.

s: peace offerings eaten with uncleanness results in being cut off from his people (for one who eats while unclean)
q: that soul shall be cut off from his people.

s: fat is forbidden to children of Israel (fat of bull, sheep, or goat)
q: You shall eat no fat, of bull, or sheep, or goat.

s: fat is burned by priests (on the altar, from peace offerings)
q: The priest shall burn the fat on the altar

s: blood is forbidden to children of Israel (bird or animal, in any dwelling; penalty is being cut off)
q: You shall not eat any blood, whether it is of bird or of animal, in any of your dwellings.

s: peace offerings (waved breast and heaved thigh) belong to Aaron (and his sons, as their portion forever)
q: the breast shall be Aaron’s and his sons’.

s: peace offerings (waved breast and heaved thigh) includes right thigh for priests (priest who offers the blood and fat)
q: He among the sons of Aaron who offers the blood of the peace offerings, and the fat, shall have the right thigh for a portion.

s: Aaron has portion from children of Israel (consecrated portion, forever throughout generations)
q: It is their portion forever throughout their generations.

s: trespass offering killed at place where burnt offering is killed (location of slaughter)
q: In the place where they kill the burnt offering, he shall kill the trespass offering

s: the LORD commanded at Mount Sinai (commanded Moses the laws of the offerings)
q: which the LORD commanded Moses in Mount Sinai

s: the LORD commands children of Israel (to offer their offerings in the wilderness of Sinai)
q: in the day that he commanded the children of Israel to offer their offerings to the LORD, in the wilderness of Sinai.

s: trespass offering has law same as sin offering (one law for both)
q: As is the sin offering, so is the trespass offering; there is one law for them.

s: trespass offering may be eaten by priests (every male, in a holy place)
q: Every male among the priests may eat of it. It shall be eaten in a holy place.

s: trespass offering belongs to priests (the priest who makes atonement with it)
q: The priest who makes atonement with them shall have it.

s: trespass offering has blood sprinkled on altar (around the altar)
q: its blood he shall sprinkle around on the altar.

s: burnt offering has skin belonging to priests (the priest who offers it)
q: The priest who offers any man’s burnt offering shall have for himself the skin of the burnt offering which he has offered.

s: meal offering belongs to Aaron's sons (every meal offering, mixed with oil or dry, shared equally)
q: Every meal offering, mixed with oil or dry, belongs to all the sons of Aaron, one as well as another.

s: peace offerings thanksgiving form accompanied by unleavened cakes and wafers (with oil)
q: he shall offer with the sacrifice of thanksgiving unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, and cakes mixed with oil.

s: Aaron has relationship to Aaron's sons (father and sons, consecrated together)
q: Take Aaron and his sons with him

s: anointing oil sanctifies Aaron (poured on his head)
q: He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, and anointed him, to sanctify him.

s: altar has part horns (blood was put on them)
q: put it around on the horns of the altar with his finger

s: altar has part vessels (also anointed)
q: anointed the altar and all its vessels

s: bull of the sin offering is brought by Aaron and his sons (they laid their hands on its head)
q: He brought the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull of the sin offering.

s: bull of the sin offering burned at outside the camp (skin, meat and dung burned there)
q: But the bull, and its skin, and its meat, and its dung, he burned with fire outside the camp, as the LORD commanded Moses.

s: ram of the burnt offering is a burnt offering (pleasant aroma, offering made by fire to the LORD)
q: It was a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma. It was an offering made by fire to the LORD

s: ram of consecration is a other ram (presented after the burnt offering ram)
q: He presented the other ram, the ram of consecration.

s: ram of consecration is a consecration offering (pleasant aroma, offering made by fire to the LORD)
q: They were a consecration offering for a pleasant aroma.

s: ordination of Aaron and his sons has duration seven days (they must stay at the door of the Tent of Meeting)
q: You shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Meeting for seven days, until the days of your consecration are fulfilled

s: ordination of Aaron and his sons takes place at Tent of Meeting (at the door)
q: Moses did as the LORD commanded him; and the congregation was assembled at the door of the Tent of Meeting.

s: Aaron wears priestly garments (tunic, sash, robe, ephod)
q: He put the tunic on him, tied the sash on him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him

s: ordination of Aaron and his sons commanded by the LORD
q: Aaron and his sons did all the things which the LORD commanded by Moses.

s: congregation (Israelite assembly) assembles at Tent of Meeting (at the door)
q: the congregation was assembled at the door of the Tent of Meeting

s: Aaron is commanded to stay at Tent of Meeting (day and night for seven days, with his sons)
q: You shall stay at the door of the Tent of Meeting day and night seven days

s: Aaron wears breastplate (contains the Urim and Thummim)
q: He placed the breastplate on him. He put the Urim and Thummim in the breastplate.

s: Aaron wears golden plate (holy crown on front of turban)
q: He set the turban on his head. He set the golden plate, the holy crown, on the front of the turban

s: Aaron's sons wear tunics, sashes and headbands (clothed by Moses)
q: Moses brought Aaron’s sons, and clothed them with tunics, and tied sashes on them, and put headbands on them

s: Moses serves as commanded agent of the LORD (acts as the LORD commanded him)
q: Moses did as the LORD commanded him

s: Moses receives breast of the ram of consecration (Moses' portion)
q: It was Moses’ portion of the ram of consecration, as the LORD commanded Moses.

s: anointing oil sanctifies tabernacle (with all that was in it)
q: Moses took the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle and all that was in it, and sanctified them.

s: anointing oil sanctifies altar (sprinkled seven times, with its vessels, basin and base)
q: He sprinkled it on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its vessels, and the basin and its base, to sanctify them.

s: Aaron offers sin offering (for himself and for the people)
q: Draw near to the altar, and offer your sin offering, and your burnt offering, and make atonement for yourself, and for the people

s: Fire (from before the LORD) consumes burnt offering (together with the fat on the altar)
q: Fire came out from before the LORD, and consumed the burnt offering and the fat upon the altar.

s: Fire (from before the LORD) comes from the LORD
q: Fire came out from before the LORD

s: sin offering has part calf (Aaron's sin offering) (for Aaron himself)
q: killed the calf of the sin offering, which was for himself.

s: sin offering has part goat (people's sin offering) (for the people)
q: took the goat of the sin offering which was for the people

s: burnt offering has part ram (burnt offering) (without defect)
q: a ram for a burnt offering, without defect

s: burnt offering has part lamb (burnt offering) (a year old, without defect)
q: a calf and a lamb, both a year old, without defect, for a burnt offering

s: peace offerings has part bull (peace offering) (for the people)
q: He also killed the bull and the ram, the sacrifice of peace offerings, which was for the people.

s: Tent of Meeting is location of what Moses commanded being brought before it
q: They brought what Moses commanded before the Tent of Meeting.

s: Aaron has Aaron's sons (assisted him with the blood)
q: The sons of Aaron presented the blood to him

s: Aaron performs atonement (for himself and for the people, as commanded by the LORD)
q: make atonement for yourself, and for the people; and offer the offering of the people, and make atonement for them, as the LORD commanded.

s: Aaron performs blessing of the people (lifted up his hands toward the people)
q: Aaron lifted up his hands toward the people, and blessed them

s: Moses commands Aaron (to offer sacrifices before the LORD)
q: he said to Aaron, “Take a calf from the herd for a sin offering, and a ram for a burnt offering, without defect, and offer them before the LORD.

s: Moses commands children of Israel (through Aaron, to bring offerings)
q: You shall speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘Take a male goat for a sin offering;

s: Moses performs blessing of the people (together with Aaron)
q: Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Meeting, and came out, and blessed the people

s: the LORD commands Moses (the offering procedure)
q: he burned upon the altar, as the LORD commanded Moses.

s: glory of the LORD appears to children of Israel (to all the people after the blessing)
q: the LORD’s glory appeared to all the people.

s: Nadab is a son of Aaron
q: Nadab and Abihu, the sons of Aaron

s: death of Nadab and Abihu has location before the LORD
q: they died before the LORD.

s: Aaron has child Eleazar (surviving son)
q: Moses spoke to Aaron, and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his sons who were left

s: Aaron has child Ithamar (surviving son)
q: Moses spoke to Aaron, and to Eleazar and to Ithamar, his sons who were left

s: Aaron has relative Uzziel (uncle)
q: the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron
